test_title: PYST 41: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Article was inserted into the Constitution by the 103rd Amendment Act to provide for EWS reservation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 15(6) and 16(6)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **103rd Amendment Act:** The **Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act, 2019** introduced provisions for reservation for the **Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** of society.
 
• This amendment added **Article 15(6)** and **Article 16(6)** to the Indian Constitution, enabling the government to provide up to **10% reservation** for EWS in educational institutions and government jobs.
 
• **Article 15(6):** It empowers the State to make special provisions for the advancement of economically weaker sections of citizens, including reservations in educational institutions. This applies to private institutions, whether aided or unaided, except for minority educational institutions under Article 30.
 
• **Article 16(6):** It provides reservation for EWS in government jobs, enabling the State to reserve up to 10% of vacancies in public employment.
 
• The amendment aims to address inequality by providing representation to economically disadvantaged individuals who do not fall under the existing reservation categories like Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC).
 
• It specifically targets individuals with an annual family income below **₹8 lakh**, excluding those who own significant agricultural land, residential properties, or other assets.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Article 15(6) and 16(6).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for EWS Reservation:**

 
 
• An individual from the general category whose annual family income is less than **₹8 lakh** qualifies for EWS reservation.
 
• Exclusions include families owning agricultural land above **5 acres**, residential property exceeding **1,000 square feet**, or plots larger than **100 square yards** in notified municipalities.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 103rd Amendment:**
 
 
• It is the first constitutional amendment to provide reservation based on economic criteria.
 
• The amendment aims to ensure inclusivity and address inequalities faced by economically weaker sections among the general category.
 
• It applies to both **central government jobs** and admissions to educational institutions, including private unaided institutions.
 
 
 
• **Legal Challenges:**
 
 
• The amendment faced criticism and legal scrutiny, with debates over whether economic reservation violates the principle of equality enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• In **2022**, the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the EWS reservation, confirming that it does not breach the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The concept of reservation in India has traditionally been based on social and educational backwardness, as outlined in Articles **15(4)** and **16(4)** for SC, ST, and OBC categories.
 
• The introduction of EWS reservation expands the scope of affirmative action to include economic criteria.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The 103rd Amendment ensures that economically weaker individuals from the general category, who were previously excluded from reservation benefits, receive representation in education and employment.
 
• This is expected to promote social justice and reduce economic disparities.
 
 

8d
